Hooked processes cannot write libxposed remote preferences. Runtime outcomes are reported as sanitized events in LSPosed logs, not stored here. An installer failure prevents another attempt in the same host process, but cannot automatically lock future processes. The module app can set persistent manual safety locks. No app content or exception messages are logged. Restart the host app after changing a lock.

Connection and scope are framework-owned. A successful configuration is not evidence that a target hook executed.
Guidance and installed app identity, without granting permissions or changing external configuration.

Install and enable HookLab in a compatible LSPosed framework (modern API 102). Review each target package, request its scope, enable each hook explicitly, verify the target version and restart the target app. A connected framework alone is not proof that a hook ran.

Scope approval comes from LSPosed, not from HookLab. Granting scope and opting in are independent. Removing scope requires confirmation. If connection or scope is unknown, no action is offered; inspect the LSPosed manager.

The MCC diamond control works only when you explicitly open it, confirm a write and authorize root. The read-only inspection does not modify MCC. An unrecognized balance file fails closed. No premium or automatic refill hook is installed.

DX-01 and DX-02 import user-selected log files via the system picker. They are not live root, logcat or LSPosed collectors. Imported lines can be correlated but cannot authenticate target hook execution. Export only sanitized evidence you have reviewed.

Raw third-party log messages are discarded by the redacted timeline. Copy and export happen only when you choose their controls; a copied report can remain visible in the Android clipboard. No background sharing is initiated from this help screen.
These controls navigate only. They never enable a hook, grant root or modify scope.
Current APK signing certificate SHA-256: %1$s (display only; not proof of runtime hooks)
Modern libxposed API 102 is required. Current framework: %1$s. Confirm the configured target app version and process separately.
HookLab does not grant scope itself, collect logs silently or prove target execution from imported lines. Root is requested only by the explicitly confirmed MCC manual control.
Signing information is the certificate installed on this device when available, not a release-provenance or security audit.

A manual request can set one recognized local MCC balance to 9. Inspection is read-only. Writes require a separate confirmation and HookLab root authorization; they may restart MCC. No automatic refill, Premium simulation or ad hooks. Synchronization may replace local changes.
